tldr: Visa TAP lets a merchant recognize an approved AI agent. The agent signs each request with RFC 9421, tagged for browsing or paying, and may add signed consumer and payment objects. It identifies agents; it moves no money.
whyItExists: Merchants block most automated traffic because they cannot tell a shopping agent acting for a real cardholder from a scraper or a fraud bot, and IP addresses or user-agent strings are weak evidence. TAP lets an agent that Visa has onboarded register a public key with Visa, and asks it to sign every request with a short-lived signature that says whether it is browsing or paying. A merchant, or the CDN in front of it, checks the signature against Visa's key directory and can then let the agent through, recognize the returning shopper and receive payment data in a signed container.

whatItIsNot.text: Not an IETF standard. TAP is a Visa specification published under Visa's own revocable Product Terms, and Visa alone changes it.
Not a payment rail. TAP identifies the agent and carries payment data; the money moves through Visa Intelligent Commerce tokens and ordinary card processing.

Not the Web Bot Auth working group draft. TAP predates the 2026-09-01 draft and differs from it: its own tags, does not require a Signature-Agent header, a mandatory nonce and Visa's own key directory.

Not the same "agentic token" as Mastercard's. Visa's agent credentials are agentic network tokens in Visa Intelligent Commerce; Mastercard Agentic Tokens are a separate Agent Pay product on another network.
Not a consent or spending-limit system. Authenticated purchase instructions (passkey or another issuer-approved method), step-up and limits live in Visa Intelligent Commerce, not in TAP.
Not mandatory for merchants. TAP does not require a merchant to adopt it, and the specification says a merchant does not necessarily have to register with a payment scheme to accept its credentials.
Not clearly open source. The sample repository's LICENSE.md binds users to Visa's terms, while the source files carry MIT-style headers; which text governs is not stated.

changedRecently.text: Visa expanded its Agentic Ready program to Asia Pacific and Latin America, live with more than 20 partners in the UK and Europe.
Visa announced the Agentic Directory of agents and merchants it has verified, and Agent Score for site readiness.
Cloudflare began treating signed agents as verified bots, split by Direct or Intermediary access.
Visa named 31 European issuers whose cardholders' agents completed live purchases at merchant websites, with merchants enabled through TAP.
eDreams ODIGEO said it uses TAP and the Agentic Directory to recognize verified agents on four travel brands (reported).
A community pull request asked to make the sample merchant verifier conform to RFC 9421; nothing has been merged since 2025-10-28.
Tempo announced TAP request attestation in the mppx SDK, with both TAP tags and an 8-minute lifetime; the code was merged on 2026-08-04 and shipped in 0.8.17 on 2026-08-10.
The IETF Web Bot Auth working group posted draft -00. TAP does not conform to it.
Release candidates of Visa's @visa/cli 5.0.0 began signing TAP requests; Visa still publishes no standalone TAP library.
Between 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-19 Visa moved its TAP pages, retired the overview page and dropped the key URL from the specification. An API reference stub labeled v1 was seen on 2026-10-19.
